title: Pressure Belts and Winds: The Engine of World Climate

questions.question: Ferrel's law states that the Coriolis effect deflects winds:
options: Right in the Northern Hemisphere and left in the Southern
Toward the nearest low pressure always
questions.rationale: Earth's rotation deflects moving air to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.question: The equatorial low-pressure belt with its calm, thundery air is nicknamed the:
questions.rationale: The doldrums mark the equatorial low, where rising moist air produces daily thunderstorms but weak surface winds.

questions.question: The subtropical high-pressure belts near 30–35° latitude are associated with:
questions.rationale: Sinking, drying air in the horse latitudes suppresses rain beneath the subtropical highs — hence the Sahara and other great deserts.

questions.question: The trade winds blow from the subtropical highs toward the equator as:
questions.rationale: Coriolis deflection turns the pole-to-equator flow into north-east trades in the Northern Hemisphere and south-east trades in the Southern.

questions.question: The stormy westerlies of 40–50°S are famously called the:
questions.rationale: Unblocked by land, the southern westerlies howl at 40–50°S as the roaring forties, deepening into the furious fifties.

questions.question: Which is a hot, dusty wind blowing from the Sahara toward the Mediterranean?
questions.rationale: The sirocco crosses from the Sahara to the Mediterranean carrying red dust that falls as blood rain; the harmattan is its West African cousin.

questions.question: The Loo of northern India is best described as:
options: A hot, dry, gusty wind of summer afternoons
questions.rationale: The Loo blows hot and dry across the northern plains on summer afternoons, notorious for heat waves.

questions.question: The calm, cloud-free centre of a tropical cyclone is the:
questions.rationale: Sinking air at the cyclone's centre produces the calm eye, ringed by the violent eye wall; the deadliest hazard is usually the storm surge.

questions.question: Temperate cyclones differ from tropical cyclones because they are:
options: Formed along the polar front from meeting air masses
questions.rationale: Extratropical cyclones are frontal, powered by the temperature contrast of colliding warm and cold air masses in mid-latitudes.

questions.question: The northward retreat of the subtropical westerly jet in early June signals:
options: The onset of winter in India
The burst of the southwest monsoon
questions.rationale: The subtropical westerly jet shifts north of the Himalaya as the monsoon sets in over India — a classic jet-stream weather link.
